newsitem.title: CANADA: Westmin Resources wage talks to resume.
newsitem.headline: Westmin Resources wage talks to resume.

text.p: Contract negotiations between Westmin Resources Ltd and workers at its Myra Falls zinc-copper mine will resume on Monday after a three-week break, company and union sources said.
The previous labor contract covering 360 workers -- members of the Canadian Auto Workers Union -- expired at midnight Friday.
Workers at the Myra Falls mine had voted 86 percent in favor of a strike in July, but no walk-out date has been set.
Bargaining in 1993 for the labor contract recently expired resulted in a 17-month lockout.
The two sides have yet to tackle differences over wage increases, but no work stoppage is expected, said Bruce McKnight, Wetmin's vice president for investor relations.
The company wants a six-year contract to replace the expired three-year deal, derong oppposionn from the union. Westmin has, however, offered to reopen wage talks after three years.
Jeff Keighley, chief negotiator for the union, said a substantial early retirement plan, not wages, was the make-or- break issue in the current round of negotiations.

Talks broke off in late July and meetings are now scheduled through September 10. Keighley said the union would not consider scheduling negotiations past that date unless significant progress had been made.
The Myra Falls mine is expected in 1997 to produce about 125,000 metric tonnes of zinc concentrate and about 65,000 tonnes of copper concentrate.
